tasks.prompt: Order the development of a new CMOM program for a municipal collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a mid size Ontario municipality building a capacity, management, operation and maintenance program from no formal program.

cards.label: Prioritize the deficiencies by risk and assign corrective actions with owners and completion dates
Implement the program elements and train staff on their assigned roles and record keeping duties
Assess capacity, condition and maintenance history to identify gaps and sanitary sewer overflow risks
Audit results against the objectives and update the program document on the set review cycle
Inventory and map all collection assets, including gravity sewers, manholes, lift stations and force mains
Review regulatory expectations and define program goals and measurable performance objectives

tasks.explanation: Goals and an asset inventory come before gap assessment, because corrective actions must be based on known assets and known risks. Implementation follows prioritization, and the audit closes the cycle by feeding updates back into the program.

tasks.prompt: Order a CMOM program audit from scope selection to corrective action closeout.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual internal audit of an operating CMOM program by a Class 2 supervisor.

cards.label: Gather overflow reports, work order records and inspection data for the audit period
Interview field and supervisory staff and observe current work practices in the field
Select the audit scope and criteria directly from the written CMOM program elements
Compare the evidence against the program criteria and rank each gap by risk
Verify each corrective action is closed and update the program document to match practice
Issue the audit report with corrective actions, named owners and due dates

tasks.explanation: An audit tests practice against the written program, so criteria and evidence come first. Findings are ranked before the report is issued, and closeout verification must precede any claim that the program has been corrected.

tasks.prompt: Order the hydraulic capacity evaluation element of a CMOM program for a growing service area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: trunk sewer and lift station capacity review triggered by new development applications.

cards.label: Enter the approved projects into the capital plan with triggers tied to development timing
Add committed development flows using the approved per unit flow allowances
Compile current dry weather and wet weather flows from basin monitoring records
Compare total projected flows against pipe and station firm capacities segment by segment
Recommend capacity projects or flow reduction measures for each flagged segment
Flag every segment projected to surcharge and rank the capacity deficiencies by severity

tasks.explanation: Capacity evaluation starts from measured flows, adds committed growth, and only then compares demand with capacity. Deficiencies must be identified and ranked before projects are recommended and programmed.

tasks.prompt: Order the management and staffing review element of a CMOM program update.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review of organization, staffing and communication lines during a CMOM program update.

cards.label: Identify coverage gaps for nights, weekends and emergency response and assign on call coverage
Record the review decisions in the program document and set the next review date
Communicate the revised structure and responsibilities to all collection staff
Review current staffing levels, certifications and vacancies against the work the program requires
Confirm the overall responsible operator designation and the supervisory chain for the collection system
Update role descriptions and the training matrix to close the identified gaps

tasks.explanation: Accountability is confirmed first, then staffing is tested against program workload. Coverage and training fixes follow from the gaps found, and the review is only complete once staff are told and the decisions are documented.

tasks.prompt: Order the build of a preventive maintenance schedule inside a CMOM operation and maintenance program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: converting a reactive work history into a scheduled preventive maintenance program for sewers and stations.

cards.label: Group the asset inventory into maintenance classes such as hotspot sewers, routine sewers and lift stations
Set a cleaning, inspection or service frequency for each class based on history and consequence of failure
Build the frequencies into a rolling annual schedule balanced across crews and seasons
Track completion and overdue items monthly and report them to the supervisor
Adjust frequencies for assets that block or fail before their scheduled service date
Generate the first cycle of preventive work orders from the approved schedule

tasks.explanation: Frequencies must be set by asset class and risk before a schedule can be built. Work orders flow from the schedule, completion is tracked, and field failures feed back into frequency adjustments.

tasks.prompt: Order the integration of condition assessment results into a CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a municipality merging several years of CCTV and manhole inspection results into its CMOM program.

cards.label: Reinspect on the planned cycle and compare new grades against the earlier grades
Schedule the assigned actions in the maintenance and capital plans
Assign each high ranked asset a rehabilitation, repair or reinspection action
Grade the condition of each asset using the program condition grading method
Collect and standardize all CCTV and manhole inspection records into the asset database
Rank assets by condition grade combined with consequence of failure

tasks.explanation: Raw inspection records must be standardized and graded before risk ranking is possible. Actions and schedules follow the ranking, and reinspection later verifies whether condition is stable or worsening.

tasks.prompt: Order the update of the overflow emergency response element after a major overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: post event review of a sanitary sewer overflow that reached a watercourse.

cards.label: Identify every step that was late, unclear or missing during the event
File the revised element in the program and record the change in the program revision log
Revise the response procedures, contact lists and notification timelines for those steps
Compare the actual response against the written response element step by step
Brief and retrain all response staff on the revised procedures
Complete the event investigation, including cause, estimated volume and response timeline

tasks.explanation: The response element can only be improved after the event is investigated and compared with what the plan required. Revisions come before retraining, and the change is closed by filing and logging the new version.

tasks.prompt: Order the information management build that supports a CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: moving collection records from paper files and spreadsheets into a single managed system.

cards.label: Clean and verify the existing asset data before any data is migrated
Run scheduled data quality checks and correct records that fail the checks
Define the required record types, including maps, inspections, work orders and overflow reports
Load the verified data into the geographic information system and work management system
Link inspection, work order and overflow records to the correct asset identifiers
Train staff to enter new records in the system at the time the work is done

tasks.explanation: Record requirements and clean source data come before migration, because loading poor data only preserves errors. Linking and training make the system usable, and routine quality checks keep it trustworthy.

tasks.prompt: Order the capital planning element that funds CMOM corrective and rehabilitation work.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: building a five year collection capital plan from CMOM assessment findings.

cards.label: Estimate quantities for each project using the defined scopes and unit rates on file
Track project delivery and carry incomplete high risk items forward into the next plan
Present the sequenced plan for approval and assign each approved project a delivery year
Sequence the projects by risk, coordination with road work and available funding
Compile the ranked deficiency and rehabilitation lists from the assessment elements
Group related deficiencies into constructible projects with defined scopes

tasks.explanation: Capital projects are built from ranked findings, not from preference. Scoping and quantity estimates precede sequencing and approval, and undelivered high risk work is carried forward rather than dropped.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator certification and training tracking cycle under Ontario Regulation 129/04 within a CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual tracking of collection operator certificates and training for a municipal crew.

cards.label: Schedule renewal training and continuing education for the flagged operators first
List every operator, their certificate class and type, and each certificate expiry date
Flag certificates expiring within the coming year and any duty and certificate mismatches
Compare each operator certificate against the class of system and duties they actually perform
Confirm renewed certificates are received and update the training and certification records
Report certification status to management and file the records for regulatory review

tasks.explanation: Tracking starts from an accurate list of certificates and duties. Mismatches and expiries are flagged before training is scheduled, and the cycle closes only when renewals are confirmed, recorded and reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual management review that closes the CMOM program year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the year end review of a CMOM program by collection management and the Class 2 supervisor.

cards.label: Review the audit findings and confirm which corrective actions remain open
Set the objectives, targets and priority work for the coming year from the gaps identified
Approve and issue the updated program document that records the new year plan
Assign the coming year actions to owners with dates and resource commitments
Compare the results against the program objectives and targets set for the year
Compile the year results for overflows, condition assessment, maintenance completion and capital delivery

tasks.explanation: The review is built on compiled results measured against the year objectives. Open audit actions are faced honestly, next year objectives grow out of the gaps, and the updated program document is issued as the record of the new plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the design of a basin flow monitoring program to support capacity and inflow studies.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a city dividing its collection system into monitoring basins for a one year study.

cards.label: Set the monitoring duration to capture dry weather periods and a range of storm sizes
Choose meter and rain gauge types matched to the site depths, velocities and study duration
Divide the system into basins bounded by trunk sewers, lift stations and natural drainage divides
Define the study questions, such as basin capacity, infiltration rates and rainfall response
Approve the monitoring plan, including data review and reporting responsibilities, before installation
Select meter sites at basin outlets where flow can be measured safely and representatively

tasks.explanation: Study questions drive basin boundaries, and boundaries drive meter locations. Equipment and duration are chosen to answer those questions, and approval of the full plan precedes any installation work.

tasks.prompt: Order a flow meter installation at a trunk sewer manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: area velocity meter installed in a 600 mm trunk sewer manhole for a basin study.

cards.label: Record the installation details, site photographs and start date in the monitoring log
Review site safety requirements and set up traffic control and confined space controls for the manhole
Program the meter with pipe dimensions, units and logging interval from the monitoring plan
Verify readings against a manual depth and velocity check taken at the site
Inspect and clean the manhole channel and confirm the pipe is suitable for the sensor mounting
Mount the sensor at the invert position specified for the meter and route the cable clear of flow

tasks.explanation: Safety controls and a clean, suitable channel come before mounting. Programming follows the plan, the installation is verified against manual measurements, and documentation closes the visit.

tasks.prompt: Order a scheduled flow meter maintenance and calibration check visit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly service visit to a long term basin flow meter site.

cards.label: Record all readings, adjustments and site conditions in the maintenance log
Download the stored data and review it for gaps, drift and flat lined readings before disturbing the meter
Replace batteries or desiccant if the service indicators show they are due
Inspect the sensor for debris, grease coating and damage and clean it as required
Take independent manual depth and velocity measurements at the sensor location
Compare the manual measurements with the meter readings and adjust the meter if it is out of tolerance

tasks.explanation: Stored data is reviewed first so problems are diagnosed before the site is disturbed. Cleaning precedes manual checks, manual checks justify any adjustment, and logging preserves the evidence for later data validation.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup of a rain gauge network for a rainfall dependent inflow study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: tipping bucket rain gauges deployed across six monitoring basins for one wet season.

cards.label: Install and level each gauge and connect it to its data logger
Record gauge locations, verification results and service dates in the study file
Verify each gauge by pouring a known volume of water and comparing the recorded tip count
Confirm each site has open sky exposure, security and safe access for servicing
Map the basins and select gauge sites that represent rainfall across the whole study area
Synchronize all logger clocks to the same time standard used by the flow meters

tasks.explanation: Representative siting comes before installation, and a gauge is not trusted until a known volume test verifies it. Matching logger clocks to the flow meters is essential because rainfall and flow records are later aligned by time.

tasks.prompt: Order the validation of one month of basin flow data before it is used in analysis.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: office review of depth, velocity and rainfall records from four basin meters.

cards.label: Release the validated data set with a validation note describing every change made
Plot depth and velocity together and flag periods where the two signals disagree
Mark unrecoverable periods as invalid so they are excluded from analysis
Correct records only where a documented cause supports the correction
Compare suspect periods against maintenance logs, rainfall records and upstream meter data
Check the records for missing intervals, clock drift and logger download errors

tasks.explanation: Validation works from raw record integrity to signal consistency to documented corrections. Invalid data is excluded rather than guessed, and the released set carries a note so later analysis can be traced.

tasks.prompt: Order a basin comparison analysis that ranks basins for further inflow and infiltration work.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twelve monitored basins compared after a full monitoring season.

cards.label: Normalize each basin result by sewer length and by number of service connections
Calculate average dry weather flow for each basin from validated dry period records
Combine the rankings with basin age, materials and overflow history
Recommend the highest ranked basins for detailed source investigation in the work plan
Rank the basins by normalized dry weather flow and by wet weather response
Calculate wet weather peaking factors for comparable storms in each basin

tasks.explanation: Basins can only be compared fairly after flows are normalized for size. Rankings from both dry and wet weather analysis, combined with asset history, determine where detailed investigation money is spent first.

tasks.prompt: Order a dry weather flow analysis for one monitored basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two rain free weeks of flow records from a residential basin.

cards.label: Read the minimum night flow between 02:00 and 05:00 as the groundwater infiltration indicator
Compare the infiltration rate with the program allowance per hectare and per kilometre of sewer
Select a rain free period with at least three antecedent dry days from the validated records
Extract the hourly flows and build the average weekday and weekend diurnal patterns
Report whether the basin passes the allowance or proceeds to source investigation
Separate the sanitary base flow from the infiltration component using the night flow and pattern shape

tasks.explanation: A defensible dry weather period must be selected before patterns are built. Night flow reveals the infiltration component, and only a separated infiltration rate can be compared with the program allowance.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather response analysis for a monitored basin after a major storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 40 mm storm event with flow and rainfall records at five minute intervals.

cards.label: Measure the pre storm dry weather flow as the baseline for the event
Classify the response as fast inflow, delayed infiltration, or a combination, from the response timing
Track the flow rise, time to peak and peak flow during and after the storm
Align the rainfall record and the basin flow record on the same time base
Compare the event response with earlier storms to confirm the basin behaviour is consistent
Calculate the rainfall dependent inflow volume above the baseline for the full event

tasks.explanation: Rainfall and flow must share a time base before any event math is valid. Baseline, peak and volume are measured in that order, the timing of the response identifies the source type, and comparison with earlier storms confirms the finding.

tasks.prompt: Order the closeout of a flow monitoring program at the end of its planned term.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: removal of eight temporary meters and delivery of the final study report.

cards.label: Archive the validated data, site records and maintenance logs in the study file
Complete the final analysis report with basin findings and recommended next steps
Present the findings to management and enter approved follow up work into the program plan
Complete a final data download and site verification reading at each meter
Remove the meters and mounting hardware and restore each manhole to its normal condition
Confirm all required storm and dry weather data targets have been captured in the validated data set

tasks.explanation: Meters are not removed until data targets are proven complete. Removal and archiving preserve the record, and the report and management presentation convert the study into funded follow up work.

tasks.prompt: Order a long term flow trending review used to update system capacity records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: five years of permanent trunk meter data reviewed by a Class 2 supervisor.

cards.label: Identify the trend rate and any step changes tied to new development or rehabilitation work
Compare projected peak flows with the recorded firm capacity of the trunk and downstream station
Plot annual average, peak day and peak hour flows against service population growth
Project flows forward to the planning horizon using the confirmed trend
Update the capacity records and flag the year when capacity action will be required
Assemble the validated annual flow summaries for the full five year period

tasks.explanation: Trending starts from validated history and separates growth trends from one time step changes. Projections are compared with firm capacity, and the capacity record is updated with the year action will be needed.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of an infiltration and inflow reduction program for a high ranked basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a basin ranked worst in the monitoring study, entering a three year reduction program.

cards.label: Group the confirmed sources into rehabilitation and disconnection projects
Confirm the basin infiltration and inflow quantities and targets from the monitoring analysis
Plan source investigations, including smoke testing, manhole inspection and lateral investigation
Divide the basin into subareas and schedule flow isolation to locate the worst subareas
Set the post project flow verification method and the program reporting schedule
Sequence the projects by cost per unit of flow removed and by coordination with other work

tasks.explanation: Targets come from measured flows, and isolation narrows the search before source investigation begins. Projects are built from confirmed sources, sequenced by value, and the program defines in advance how success will be verified.

tasks.prompt: Order a night flow isolation step test to locate infiltration in a basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: overnight step testing of a basin between 01:00 and 05:00 using temporary plugs and a downstream meter.

cards.label: Calculate the infiltration rate for each segment from its flow drop and sewer length
Rank the segments and release the worst segments for detailed source investigation
Confirm dry weather and low groundwater conditions are suitable and notify the on call supervisor
Isolate the first upstream branch with a plug and record the flow drop after it stabilizes
Move the isolation point branch by branch, recording the flow drop for each segment
Record the starting basin flow at the downstream meter with all branches open

tasks.explanation: A stable starting flow is the reference for every later measurement. Each branch is isolated in turn so its flow drop can be credited to that segment, and segment rates drive the ranking for investigation.

tasks.prompt: Order a smoke testing program for one basin, from planning to confirmed defects.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: smoke testing of 4 km of sanitary sewer in a residential basin to find inflow sources.

cards.label: Introduce smoke and walk the section recording every emission point with photographs and locations
Isolate the test section with plugs and confirm the blower setup at the starting manhole
Notify residents and the fire service of the testing area and dates and deliver door notices
Issue repair notices for public defects and notification letters for private defects
Reinspect repaired locations and record confirmed source removals in the program file
Classify each emission as a public defect, a private defect, or a normal plumbing vent

tasks.explanation: Notification protects residents and responders before smoke is introduced. Emissions are only useful once classified by ownership, notices follow classification, and reinspection confirms the sources were actually removed.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole inspection program aimed at infiltration and inflow sources.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspection of 300 manholes in an old basin with high groundwater.

cards.label: Photograph and measure active infiltration at joints, connections and the chimney
Verify completed work during wet conditions and record the infiltration stopped
Inspect each manhole from the surface and inside where safe, recording defects by component
Group the graded manholes into sealing, lining and replacement work packages
Assign each manhole a condition grade and a rehabilitation method for its defects
Prioritize manholes by age, material, depth below groundwater and location in the worst flow segments

tasks.explanation: Inspection order follows risk, and each manhole record separates defect type by component. Grading drives the repair method, work is packaged for delivery, and wet weather verification proves the infiltration was stopped.

tasks.prompt: Order the analysis that separates rainfall dependent infiltration from direct inflow in a basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: office analysis using one season of five minute rainfall and flow data.

cards.label: Subtract the baseline from each storm hydrograph to isolate the rainfall dependent volume
Direct the fast component to surface and roof source investigations and the slow component to pipe and joint investigations
Divide the response into fast, medium and slow components by time from the start of rain
Attribute the fast component mainly to direct inflow and the slow component mainly to rainfall dependent infiltration
Select a set of storms of different sizes and durations from the validated rainfall record
Build the dry weather baseline pattern for the basin from rain free periods

tasks.explanation: Storm selection and a solid baseline come first, because the rainfall dependent volume is defined as flow above that baseline. Splitting the response by timing is what allows sources to be assigned to the right investigation program.

tasks.prompt: Order a dye testing investigation of suspected private inflow sources on one street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dye testing of roof leaders and a catch basin suspected of cross connection to the sanitary sewer.

cards.label: Document each confirmed connection and issue the correction notice for that property
Repeat the test source by source, flushing clear water between tests to avoid carryover
Confirm the downstream sanitary manhole is monitored by a crew member in radio contact
Introduce dyed water into the first suspect source at a controlled rate
Record whether dye appears in the sanitary manhole and the time it takes to appear
Obtain permission for property access and notify the occupants of the test timing

tasks.explanation: Access and a monitored downstream manhole must be in place before any dye is used. Testing one source at a time with flushing between tests keeps results attributable, and confirmed connections are documented for correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the prioritization of rehabilitation projects inside an inflow and infiltration reduction program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twenty candidate projects competing for one year of program funding.

cards.label: Rank the projects by cost effectiveness, adjusted for overflow risk and structural condition
Estimate the rehabilitation quantity and cost for each candidate project
Calculate the cost per unit of flow removed for every project
Select the funded set that removes the most flow within the approved budget
Record the unfunded projects in priority order for the next funding cycle
Confirm the flow contribution of each candidate source from isolation and investigation records

tasks.explanation: Prioritization is only defensible when flow removed and cost are both known for each project. Cost effectiveness ranks the list, risk adjusts it, and unfunded projects are preserved in order rather than lost.

tasks.prompt: Order the post rehabilitation flow verification for a completed reduction project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a basin where lining and manhole sealing were completed the previous construction season.

cards.label: Confirm rehabilitation records are complete and all sources in the project scope were addressed
Reinstall basin flow meters at the same locations used for the original study
Monitor through comparable dry periods and storms matched to the original study conditions
Report the verified result and carry any shortfall sources into the next program phase
Compare the measured reduction against the project target reduction
Calculate the new infiltration and inflow rates using the same method as the original study

tasks.explanation: Verification repeats the original measurement at the same locations under comparable conditions, because only a like for like comparison proves reduction. Shortfalls are not hidden; they become the next phase of work.

tasks.prompt: Order a private source removal and verification cycle for one neighbourhood.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: forty properties with confirmed downspout and foundation drain connections to the sanitary sewer.

cards.label: Send each owner a notice describing the confirmed connection, the required correction and the deadline
Inspect each completed disconnection and confirm storm flows are directed to an approved outlet
Update the basin source inventory and credit the removed flows in the program totals
Offer a pre correction visit to confirm the disconnection method for each property
Record owner commitments and schedule follow up inspections by street
Retest non responding properties and escalate to the enforcement process in the program bylaw

tasks.explanation: Owners are notified and supported before enforcement is considered. Inspections confirm each correction, escalation is reserved for non response, and the inventory update credits only verified removals.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual progress report for a multi year inflow and infiltration reduction program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: year two report of a five year basin reduction program to municipal management.

cards.label: Recommend target, budget or method changes for the remaining program years
Present the report and record the approved changes in the program plan
Compare spending to date against the flow removed and the original program targets
Compile verified flow reductions from the post project monitoring results
Explain variances, including sources that cost more or removed less flow than expected
Compile the sources found, corrected and remaining from the program inventory

tasks.explanation: The report is built from inventory and verified monitoring, not from activity counts alone. Spending is judged against measured flow removed, variances are explained, and recommendations close the loop into the approved plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual planning of a CCTV condition assessment program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a municipality planning one year of mainline CCTV inspection across several basins.

cards.label: Set the inspection specification, including defect coding, deliverables and data format
Confirm which selected sewers need cleaning before inspection and schedule that cleaning first
Schedule crews and equipment so cleaned sewers are inspected promptly before debris returns
Select the inspection areas using asset age, material, failure history and program priorities
Define the supervisory review sample and the acceptance checks for delivered video and data
Publish the annual plan with monthly production targets by basin

tasks.explanation: Area selection uses risk and history, and cleaning must be scheduled ahead of cameras because debris hides defects. The specification and review rules are set before production starts so delivered data can be accepted or rejected against them.

tasks.prompt: Order a CCTV crew workday from setup to accepted daily deliverables.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one crew inspecting 250 mm residential sewers on a scheduled program day.

cards.label: Verify camera calibration and enter the header information for the first inspection
Set up traffic control and open the starting manhole, confirming the sewer is cleaned and flowing normally
Review the day work package, maps and traffic control requirements at the start of shift
Transfer the day video and data and confirm the office received complete files
Complete the defect coding for each inspection before leaving the setup
Run the inspection at a controlled speed, stopping and panning at every defect and connection

tasks.explanation: The work package and site setup come before the camera enters the pipe. Header accuracy and in field coding keep each inspection traceable, and the day is not complete until the office confirms receipt of the full record.

tasks.prompt: Order the supervisory review of CCTV defect coding for one week of delivered inspections.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a Class 2 supervisor reviewing contractor delivered inspections for acceptance.

cards.label: Return inspections with coding errors to the contractor with the required corrections noted
Select a review sample that includes the highest grade defects and a random share of routine inspections
Accept the corrected inspections and load them into the condition database
Confirm structural and maintenance defect types, clock positions and severity grades
Play each sampled inspection and compare the video against the coded defects
Summarize recurring coding errors and brief the contractor and in house crews on the corrections

tasks.explanation: Review compares codes against the actual video, with the most serious defects checked first. Corrections are returned and rechecked before acceptance, and recurring errors are fed back as training so quality improves.

tasks.prompt: Order the conversion of CCTV condition grades into a rehabilitation candidate list.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three years of graded inspections being converted into a candidate project list.

cards.label: Group adjacent high grade sewers into project reaches that can be built as one contract
Combine the condition grades with consequence scores for road class, depth and overflow history
Assign a likely rehabilitation method to each reach from its defect pattern
Rank the reaches by combined condition and consequence for capital planning
Hold the ranked list as candidates until field verification confirms the top reaches
Extract all sewers with the highest structural grades and active infiltration defects

tasks.explanation: The candidate list starts from the worst condition grades, then consequence and grouping turn individual sewers into buildable projects. Ranking supports capital planning, but field verification still confirms the top reaches before design money is spent.

tasks.prompt: Order an emergency CCTV investigation of a suspected sewer collapse under a road.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a road depression over a trunk sewer reported by the roads department.

cards.label: Inspect the manholes upstream and downstream for deformation, debris and flow condition
Close or control traffic over the depression and make the work area safe
Mark the surface location of any collapse or major deformation found
Review records for the sewer age, material, depth and repair history at that location
Run CCTV from the downstream manhole toward the suspect area as far as the camera can safely travel
Report the findings to the supervisor for excavation and repair planning the same day

tasks.explanation: Public safety and records come first, manhole checks frame what the camera should find, and the camera run locates the failure. Surface marking and same day reporting convert the investigation into a repair decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the manhole condition assessment workflow used beside the CCTV program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: structured manhole inspections completed in the same basins as the CCTV program.

cards.label: Inspect and photograph each component in order from cover and frame down to the benching and invert
Record defects, infiltration and corrosion for each component with measurements where required
Forward manholes with safety or structural concerns for supervisory review and action
Enter the record into the asset database linked to the manhole identifier the same day
Open and ventilate the manhole and complete atmospheric testing before any entry or internal inspection
Assign the manhole condition grade from the worst component scores using the program method

tasks.explanation: Atmospheric safety precedes inspection, and components are assessed in a fixed top to bottom order so nothing is missed. Grading follows the recorded defects, and safety concerns are escalated rather than left in the database.

tasks.prompt: Order the coordination of sewer cleaning ahead of a CCTV inspection contract.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a contractor CCTV program where the municipality cleans sewers in advance.

cards.label: Schedule cleaning crews far enough ahead of the camera crews to keep a buffer of ready reaches
Close the reach in the tracking system only when the accepted inspection is received
Clean each reach and record the debris type and amount removed in the work record
Reinspect any reach where the camera finds debris above the specification limit and reclean it
Notify the CCTV contractor which reaches are released as ready for inspection
Identify the inspection reaches that records and history show carry heavy debris or grease

tasks.explanation: Cleaning is targeted by history and scheduled with a buffer so cameras never wait or film dirty pipe. Reaches are released in writing, failed reaches are recleaned, and closure waits for an accepted inspection.

tasks.prompt: Order the acceptance inspection of a rehabilitated sewer using post construction CCTV.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: acceptance of a lined reach before the rehabilitation contract is closed.

cards.label: Run the acceptance CCTV and compare the video against the acceptance criteria in the specification
List every defect that fails the criteria as a deficiency for the contractor to correct
Reinspect the corrected sections and confirm each deficiency is resolved
Check for liner defects such as wrinkles, lifts, blisters and defective service reinstatements
Accept the reach, file the video record and release the contract holdback process
Confirm the required curing or installation period has passed and the reach is cleaned and ready

tasks.explanation: Acceptance waits until the installation is ready to be judged. The video is compared with written criteria, failures become a deficiency list, and holdback release follows only after corrections are reinspected and the reach is accepted.

tasks.prompt: Order the quality check of CCTV data before it is loaded into the asset management system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, permits where they apply, and standard collection practice in the cited sources.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly data load of program inspections into the municipal asset system.

cards.label: Return failed records to the producer with the specific errors listed
Check that every inspection file has a matching video, header record and coded defect file
Run validation checks for impossible values such as lengths beyond the mapped segment length
Load the corrected and passed records into the asset management system
Verify asset identifiers, street names and upstream and downstream manhole references
Run a post load sample check to confirm the loaded records display correctly

tasks.explanation: Completeness and identifier checks come before validation rules, because a perfect file attached to the wrong asset is still an error. Only passed and corrected records are loaded, and a post load sample confirms the load itself worked.
